tool_calls.name: universe_describe
tool_calls.result_text:
v_demand
  workcell (VARCHAR): Workcell = customer — resolved through the registry, never the planner's raw spelling.
  workcell_id (INTEGER): Join key to v_workcell.
  assembly (VARCHAR): Part number = model = assembly — the key the planner and cycle time are joined on (case 18).
  model_id (BIGINT): Join key to dim_model.
  period_start (DATE): Start of the planning period (Monday for weeks).
  period_type (VARCHAR): week (13-week planner) or month.
  qty (DOUBLE): Units planned in the period.
  source (VARCHAR): Which planner sheet the number came from.
  as_of (DATE): The date the planner snapshot was taken — demand changes every week; say which snapshot.

tool_calls.name: universe_describe
tool_calls.result_text:
v_workcell
  workcell_id (BIGINT): The one id for a workcell. Every other table joins on this, never on a name.
  workcell (VARCHAR): Workcell = CUSTOMER — the customer-dedicated production organisation (e.g. KEYSIGHT, WABTEC). Not a station, not a cell on a line.
  entity_type (VARCHAR): customer = a normal customer workcell · shared_line = an internal line many customers use (AOP runs SMT for others) · support = has people, builds nothing (WAREHOUSE) · unknown = the row scans land on when no customer resolves.
  status (VARCHAR): active or inactive in the August 2026 registry. 'How many workcells' has several true answers — say which filter you used.
  plant_physical (VARCHAR): Where the workcell physically sits: P1, P2 or BK (Batu Kawan). MICRON SIG, LAMGB, LAMMEC sit in BK.
  plant_governing (VARCHAR): Which plant supervises it. Differs from plant_physical for MICRON SIG, LAMGB, LAMMEC (BK floor, Plant 1 supervision). 'In P1' is two questions — ask which.
  region (VARCHAR): Penang Island (P1 + P2) or Batu Kawan, following the physical plant.
  division (VARCHAR): MES division text, an attribute of the workcell, not a level above it.
  mes_customer_id (DOUBLE): The primary MES Customer_ID. Some workcells hold two (KEYSIGHT is 7 and 114) — the full set is in workcell_alias.
  parent_proposed (VARCHAR): The parent workcell the August registry PROPOSED (KEYSIGHT for K_CTEC …). Families are not yet a confirmed fact; do not roll up on this without saying so.
  confidence (VARCHAR): extracted = seen in source data · guess = inferred by the August registry build · n/a = synthetic row.

answer:
I couldn’t find any column that tells me how many bays a workcell has.  
The only view that contains work‑cell‑level information is **v_workcell**, and its columns are:

| Column | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| workcell | Customer name (e.g. KEYSIGHT) |
| workcell_id | Primary key |
| entity_type | customer / shared_line / support / unknown |
| status | active / inactive |
| plant_physical | Physical plant (P1, P2, BK) |
| plant_governing | Governing plant |
| region | Penang Island or Batu Kawan |
| division | MES division text |
| mes_customer_id | MES Customer_ID(s) |
| parent_proposed | Proposed parent workcell |
| confidence | extraction confidence |

None of these columns records the number of bays, nor is there a separate “bay” table in the Jabil Universe.  
Because the bay count is not available, I cannot simulate how many demands would overload or break the KEYSIGHT workcell. If you can provide a source that lists bay counts, I can then compare that to the demand and capacity data.
